I can’t edit the image here (no image tools), and I won’t claim an edited bitmap was produced. Below are clear, non‑destructive step‑by‑step methods you can follow in common tools to replace the plain gray background with blue while leaving the person untouched.

Recommended blue colors (pick one): #1E90FF (DodgerBlue), #007BFF, #0D47A1 (deep blue), #87CEEB (sky blue).

Photoshop (CC)
1. Duplicate the Background layer (Layer → Duplicate Layer).
2. With the duplicate selected: Select → Subject.
3. Click Select and Mask…:
   - Use Refine Edge Brush over hair/edges.
   - Smooth 0–10, Feather 0.5–3 px (adjust by resolution), Shift Edge ±1–3% as needed.
   - Output To: Layer Mask. Click OK.
4. Create a Solid Color Fill layer (Layer → New Fill Layer → Solid Color) and choose your blue. Place this fill layer underneath the masked duplicate layer.
5. Inspect edges at 100% zoom. If you see gray fringing, on the masked layer double‑click the mask → Properties → check “Decontaminate Colors” (or use “Defringe” on duplicated layer). Use a small brush on the mask to clean remaining halo.
6. If there was a natural shadow on the gray background you want to keep, make sure your selection preserved it; otherwise paint a soft black on a new layer under the subject, blur, lower opacity, and set Multiply to match.

GIMP
1. Duplicate the image layer.
2. With duplicate active, use the Foreground Select Tool (or Select → By Color and click the gray).
3. Refine the selection (paint to refine foreground), then Select → To Mask (Layer → Mask → Add Layer Mask → Selection).
4. Add a new layer under the masked layer, fill it with your chosen blue.
5. Clean mask edges with a soft paintbrush on the mask; use Filters → Blur → Gaussian Blur (very small radius) if edges look too hard.

Affinity Photo
- Use Select Person (or Selection Brush) → Refine → Output as Mask. Add a fill layer underneath and choose blue. Use Refine to fix hair and edge fringing.

Online quick way (no desktop app)
1. Use remove.bg (or similar) to produce a PNG with a transparent background.
2. Open the PNG in Canva / Figma / Photopea / any editor, add a blue rectangle layer beneath the PNG, export.

Command line (ImageMagick sketch)
- Make the gray pixels transparent (adjust fuzz to tolerate lighting variation), then composite over a blue background. Example sketch (test and adjust -fuzz):
  magick input.jpg -fuzz 8% -transparent "#808080" temp.png
  magick temp.png -background "#1E90FF" -flatten output.png
- Test different -fuzz values (4%–12%) and check edges. This approach can produce halos; follow up with small blur/shrink on the alpha if needed.

Edge handling tips (general)
- Work non‑destructively (masks, duplicated layers).
- Zoom to 100% to check hair/fine edges. Use refine edge brushes or manual mask painting to preserve fine detail.
